summary: You have a clear and well-motivated concept. Your explanation of why reef monitoring matters, and of the value of a near-real-time relay to ground stations, is easy to follow. The main problem is the orbit: a geostationary orbit must be about 35,786 km above the equator, so it cannot hover over the Great Barrier Reef at 600 km. Fixing this, along with the plan inconsistency and the thin preliminary results, will raise your work considerably.
next_steps: Correct the orbit choice so it is technically valid and justify it against the reef's latitude and your coverage and latency needs. Also revise the bleaching explanation so it names thermal stress as the primary driver.
Make the project plan consistent: align the text on weeks 7 to 8 with the Gantt chart's weeks 9 to 10, and add contingencies for likely delays or design variations.
Present preliminary results for your corrected orbit, such as STK outputs with a short interpretation, and replace the URL footnotes with a full reference list.

criteria.C1: You clearly describe the mission concept and why reef monitoring matters, including the reef's value for food, protection, jobs and tourism. Your relay to ground stations is well motivated. To reach the higher level, define measurable objectives and requirements, such as revisit time, spatial resolution and data latency. Broaden your users beyond scientists to include reef managers and other decision-makers. Correct the bleaching claim, since thermal stress is the main driver, and use a full reference list.
criteria.C2: Your weekly Gantt chart with deadlines and task descriptions makes the plan look feasible. To reach the higher level, add contingencies and variations, and explain why the sequence suits the mission. Name your information sources specifically. Resolve the conflict between the text (weeks 7 and 8) and the chart (weeks 9 and 10). The orbit error also weakens the link between your plan and the mission concept.
criteria.C3: You have made progress: you completed STK tutorials 1 to 4 and reviewed the Asner Hawaii monitoring brief. However, no results, orbit analysis or STK outputs are yet presented or interpreted. Add preliminary results for your corrected orbit, such as ground tracks, coverage or pass-time outputs, with a brief interpretation of what they show about your design and whether you are on track.
criteria.C4: Your headings, consistent footnotes and readable Gantt chart give the report a clear structure. To reach the higher level, tighten the phrasing, which is sometimes awkward. Give the Gantt chart a formal figure caption and refer to it in the text. Fix the editing-week contradiction. Replace URL footnotes with a reference list that matches your in-text citations.
